items.title: Al Gafa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 2, 2023
items.q: They wrote many Ray Charles hits and Andy Williams.

ctx.x: I love that. “We can’t start the session yet, Al’s on his way from high school.” You know this was on my list of topics because I’m fascinated by those recording sessions at the time. You had stated that in the early 60s money was being thrown around in the music business. Can you extrapolate on that a little bit?

Okay yeah. First of all my recording work started — I auditioned with a, it was a doo- wop group. They had an audition with two really well known artists, Doc Pomus and Morty Shuman. They wrote many Ray Charles hits and Andy Williams. They went to play an audition and they asked me to play the audition with them. And at the audition Morty Shuman, he was the keyboard player, he asked me if I would like to do recording sessions. So I’m just — it was a hobby of mine, yeah sure, okay, what’s a recording session?…
Those first sessions, like that first audition, did they put music in front of you? Chord charts or what? © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-
